body.statement: The entire penalized-regret path has the uniform second-order reduction \(\sup_{c\in\mathcal C}|nR_n(c)-\tfrac12\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}^\top H_c\{n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi^\theta_c(O_i)\}|=o_{\mathbb P}(1)\), so \(nR_n\Rightarrow Q\) in \(C(\mathcal C)\). Conditionally on the data, the totalized process \(Q_n^*\Rightarrow Q\), and conditional quantiles of continuous supremum functionals of \(Q_n^*\), enlarged by the fixed slack \(\eta\), yield simultaneous upper bands for \(R_n(c)\) that remain valid at \(\widehat c\). On the common regular finite-action benchmark-centered softmax submodel, set FangRidderXie2026's optimization penalty to \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\), so its reported preference is \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\). This process is the uniform-in-penalty extension of its Theorem 2 fixed-penalty quadratic-regret law and its Theorem 5 efficient doubly robust quadratic-regret limit.
body.justification: Under the note's explicitly stronger path-uniform smoothness and curvature conditions, the same first-order policy noise determines second-order loss across preferences, so separate fixed-positive-penalty regret approximations cannot support curve selection.
body.gap: FangRidderXie2026 Theorem 2 gives the quadratic-regret law at one fixed optimization penalty \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}>0\), and Theorem 5 gives the efficient doubly robust optimizer and quadratic-regret limit. On the common finite-action benchmark-centered softmax subclass, with \(\lambda_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c\) and \(c_{\mathrm{FRX}}=c/s_W^{\mathrm{FRX}}\), this theorem extends those fixed-penalty conclusions uniformly over the direct penalty path and adds conditionally valid shared-multiplier calibration; ChenFang2019 explains why a naive standard bootstrap is not enough.
body.consumer: A planner choosing a displayed commitment-savings tradeoff receives a simultaneous upper bound on the statistical penalized-welfare loss of the fitted rule.
